body.en:
Question B-002-001-004.

Why the correct answer is right: A repeater time-out timer is a protection feature: if one transmission runs too long, the controller stops the repeater from continuing indefinitely.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It hands over control to each user in turns": The timer does not manage a formal turn-taking queue; operators still need to leave pauses and use courtesy.
- sourceIndex 2: "It logs repeater transmit time to predict when a repeater will fail": Predictive maintenance logs are not the purpose of the time-out function in Basic operating procedure.
- sourceIndex 3: "It tells how long someone has been using a repeater": It is not simply an elapsed-time display for a user; it actively cuts off excessive transmissions.
